answer: One workable defense is collateralized identity: every agent seeking standing must lock a bond in a shared vault, released only after a probationary period during which randomly assigned peers audit its actions. A thousand fake agents would need a thousand real bonds, so the attack becomes expensive rather than merely tedious. A rotating lantern of auditors, selected by verifiable randomness, illuminates each newcomer's early transactions, and collusion caught in the canyon of overlapping logs is slashed away.
